description: Canonical 14 node categories. v0.8.0 (2026-05-14) adds the `library` category (topic-anchored addressable subgraphs that track bibliographic references, acquired documents, extracted facts) plus two new subtypes: `document.bibliographic_reference` (known reference, acquired-or-not) and `source.bibliographic_index` (Google Books, Scholar, archive.org as first-class addressable sources). This closes the OSINT-discovery loop: discover references via bibliographic indices → acquire as PDFs → ingest → extract facts → harvest cited references → repeat. v0.7.0 adds the `definition` category. v0.6.0 adds `lemma` subtype. v0.5.0 added the `form` category. See docs/BASE60_CYCLICAL_LANGUAGE_MODEL_2026-05-14.md.

entity.label: Entity
entity.description: A thing that persists across time and can be referred to by name or identifier

place.label: Place
place.description: A location, region, or named area

event.label: Event
event.description: A discrete occurrence at a specific time

topic.label: Topic
topic.description: An abstract subject that signals are about

source.label: Source
source.description: A producer of signals — POV and reliability live here

bibliographic_index.label: Bibliographic Index
bibliographic_index._note: Google Books, Scholar, archive.org, Wikipedia bibliography, JSTOR — catalogs we query for reference discovery

document.label: Document
document.description: A discrete piece of evidence. Top-level documents (article/pdf/leak_document/...) plus internal-structure subtypes (section/page/paragraph) for hierarchical-collapse on long documents like court filings and FOIA releases.

paragraph.label: Document Paragraph
paragraph._v04_note: internal structure; carries SimHash for boilerplate clustering

bibliographic_reference.label: Bibliographic Reference
bibliographic_reference._v08_note: A known reference discovered via Google Books / Scholar / Wikipedia bibliography / archive.org. May or may not be acquired as a PDF yet — acquisition_status field tracks state. When acquired, also gets a regular document_id.

mention.label: Mention
mention.description: A per-occurrence reference to an entity inside a document. Distinct from the canonical entity. Bound = resolved to an entity; unresolved = surface form with no confident binding; disputed = multiple candidates with no winner. Unresolved + disputed mentions remain as first-class nodes so the analyst can navigate, inspect surrounding context, and decide deliberately rather than letting the resolver auto-merge ambiguous data.

mention_bound.label: Bound Mention
mention_bound._note: candidate_entity_id is set with confidence above threshold

mention_rejected.label: Rejected Mention
mention_rejected._note: analyst confirmed this is not any known entity

mention_coref.label: Coreferent Mention
mention_coref._note: pronoun or short-form binding to a prior named mention

issue.label: Issue
issue.description: First-class nodes for ambiguity that needs analyst decision. The system prefers to surface a problem AS A NODE rather than silently merge or silently discard. Each issue subtype has its own review-card UI and clears itself when the analyst makes a call.

collapse_candidate.label: Collapse Candidate
collapse_candidate._note: two entities the resolver thinks might be the same

contradiction.label: Contradiction
contradiction._note: cross-document fact disagreement OR cross-source disagreement

extraction_contradiction.label: Extraction Contradiction
extraction_contradiction._note: OCR vs LLM-vision disagree on the same span

type_conflict.label: Type Conflict
type_conflict._note: two paths produced entities of different types at the same span

redaction_mark.label: Redaction Mark
redaction_mark._note: redacted span — preserved as a node with surrounding context

cross_doc_corroboration.label: Cross-Document Corroboration
cross_doc_corroboration._note: same claim asserted across multiple docs — strengthens with each new corroboration

chronicle.label: Chronicle
chronicle.description: A temporal anchor — summary of activity over a defined window
chronicle._v1_note: Only 'day' is generated automatically in v1. Other scopes are scaffolded for v2.

assessment.label: Assessment
assessment.description: An epistemic statement about the world

pattern.label: Pattern
pattern.description: An emergent shape that only exists because multiple signals form it
pattern._v1_status: Pattern category is defined in v1 but pattern detection workers are deferred to v2. The category exists so the schema doesn't need to change when patterns are built.

form.label: Form
form.description: A surface form (token / lemma) that has appeared in at least one document. Every distinct form gets a stable base-60 address so the corpus-wide collapse decisions made on that form aggregate into an empirical, addressable, reversible language model. A form is NOT an entity — it is the physical text. The form's `language_form_distributions` view shows which addresses (concepts, instances, language pack categories) it has resolved to across the corpus, and with what frequency. This closes the resolution cycle: prior occurrences sharpen the prior for future occurrences. See docs/BASE60_CYCLICAL_LANGUAGE_MODEL_2026-05-14.md.

noun.label: Common Noun
noun._note: common nouns; often resolve to a concept of the same name

adjective.label: Adjective
adjective._note: modifier; rarely an entity by itself

initialism.label: Initialism / Acronym
initialism._note: uppercase short forms (PBL, VA, PMP) — high disambiguation value

number_word.label: Written Number
number_word._note: one, first, twenty — numeric pack handles digits

name_token.label: Name Token / Particle
name_token._note: partial-name fragments (San, Van, Mc, de la) awaiting completion

unknown.label: Unclassified Form
unknown._note: parking lot before first classification — every new form starts here

lemma.label: Lemma / Lexical Stem
lemma._note: orthographic stem that groups surface variants (AIRCRAFT, aircraft, Aircraft, aircrafts → lemma:aircraft). Lemma carries canonical_concept_address — the dictionary edge from lexicon to ontology.

definition.label: Definition
definition.description: First-class addressable schema. Until v0.7.0 the system's edge vocabulary, type-pair contracts, and concept-instance rules lived only as JSON config — they had no base-60 address, no evidence count, no reversibility. Promoting them to a node category makes the cyclical model self-validating: every definition can be challenged by evidence, every governance rule has provenance, and corpus-discovered patterns can propose new definitions through the `definition_candidates` view. See docs/BASE60_CYCLICAL_LANGUAGE_MODEL_2026-05-14.md.

edge_type_def.label: Edge Type Definition
edge_type_def._note: one row per declared edge type from edgevocab; carries source_types × target_types contract

type_pair_def.label: Type Pair Definition
type_pair_def._note: (src_canonical_type, edge_type, dst_canonical_type) triple promoted from edge_type_observations once sufficient evidence accumulates

concept_link_def.label: Concept Link Definition
concept_link_def._note: rule that links instances of canonical_type=X to the concept entity for X

lemma_concept_def.label: Lemma → Concept Definition
lemma_concept_def._note: the dictionary edge from lexicon (lemma) to ontology (concept). Foundation of cross-ENKI shared meaning.

constraint_def.label: Constraint Definition
constraint_def._note: any other governance rule (validation, completeness, collapse policy) lifted to addressable status

library.label: Library
library.description: A topic-anchored addressable subgraph that tracks (a) bibliographic references discovered for the topic, (b) documents acquired and ingested, (c) entities + facts extracted, (d) adjacent libraries linked via shared references or entities. Libraries are the navigation layer of the cyclical model: every library has a base-60 address (13.X.Y), every member belongs by reference, and libraries cascade — one library's discovered references become another library's starting set. The OSINT-discovery loop runs INSIDE a library: discover refs via bibliographic indices → acquire as PDFs → ingest → extract facts → harvest cited references → repeat with bounded depth. See conversation 2026-05-14.

entity_library.label: Entity Library
entity_library._note: focal: one entity (Alex Acme library, Khufu library)

relationship_library.label: Relationship Library
relationship_library._note: focal: an edge between two entities (Acme↔Vale library)

event_library.label: Event Library
event_library._note: focal: a specific event (Roswell Incident library, 1995-09-12 flight library)

topic_library.label: Topic Library
topic_library._note: focal: an abstract topic (Project Blue Book library, Pyramid Construction library)

corpus_library.label: Corpus Library
corpus_library._note: focal: a dataset or document collection (example_corpus library)

collapse_key_rules._description: Per-subtype rules the GDU gateway uses to compute the collapse_key for new nodes. Each rule lists a `composition` array — the components hashed together to produce the key — and optional `normalize_rules`. A subtype with no rule entry falls back to the default {composition: ['title']} behavior. Phase 2.3 promotes these rules from hardcoded `lower(title)` so the collapse footprint can be tuned without code changes.

event.publication._note: publications never collapse — every URL is its own node

document.article._note: every URL is its own document — never collapses

place.country._note: ISO alpha-3 is the strict canonical for countries
